details: Painter of Bari 8010, Southern Italy, 350-340 B.C.E. Purchase, 2013
overview_text: This pelike depicts the use of a mobility aid: a staff or cane. In ancient Greece, staff-like objects were also symbols of power, authority and justice. Archaeological narratives are selective about how these artefacts are interpreted, often rejecting the possibility of disability coinciding with symbols of power.
audio_description: This large ceramic vessel has a wide, thick rim upon a flared neck. A line of leaf-like decorations wraps around the neck. It has one handle on either side, starting below the rim and meeting at the shoulder of the vessel, which becomes a wide, bulbous body upon a circular base. The vessel is black in colour with a light orange scene in the centre. The scene depicts two young men facing each other. Both men are barefoot, have curly hair and wear large toga-style tunics that cover their bodies to the ankle, draping across one shoulder and leaving the other exposed. The man on the left is holding a long staff with his right hand; his arm is bent at the elbow. His right leg is outlined by the fabric and appears to be slightly bent forward, while his right shoulder is facing downwards, as if he is being supported by this staff. The other figure holds a shorter, curved object with his right hand around shoulder height; his arm is bent at the elbow. The two figures are standing on a geometric pattern above the vessel base and are framed by swirling patterns on either side.

details: Possibly Rhodian, c.500-400 B.C.E. Bequest of Graham Joyner, 2008.
audio_description: This mould-made ceramic figure is of a person, reclining on their left side upon a chaise-like base. The bodily and facial features are unclear due to the softness of the moulding. There are remnants of pink-red, cream and yellow coloured paint, heavily worn on the base, back and legs of the figure.

details: Boston, c.1997. Purchased in 1997. Copy of Etruscan bronze, c.525-500 BCE, 01.7482, from the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
audio_description: A bronze figurine of a woman, fixed to a modern wooden block base. The figure is wearing a long dress that is fitted to the body, and a headdress; the hood or hair is shaped to a rounded point behind her head. The figure’s arms are held out wide with sleeves flaring slightly at the elbows. The left hand is held up with the palm facing outwards; the right is also held away from the body, but the palm faces down. The figure’s left foot is further forward than the right, and the heel of the right foot is slightly lifted to give the impression they are moving. The fabric of their dress appears slightly stretched around the legs, and several incised lines detail the head, face, neckline and dress.

A human figure kneeling and holding a drum with both hands at the front and centre of their body between waist and chest height. The figure is likely mould made and faces forward with the rendered impression of a human face. In several places, there are remnants of blue and black paint, with black lines concentrating around the top of the head, the neck and above the knees. The kilt-like skirt appears to have been painted to knee length with a large patch of blue pigment still extant below the waist.

details: Mesopotamia, Greek seated figurine, c.3000 B.C.E. Purchased in 2003.
audio_description: A ceramic statuette of a seated human figure. The object is possibly mould-made and is placed on a (modern) black base. The figure wears a tall, circular headdress and soft moulding suggests facial features, but not in detail. The figure’s arms, torso and legs are shaped, although the object appears more worn from the waist down. The figure is seated upright. The top of the chair finishes just behind the figure's shoulders, touching the nape of the neck. The arms of the chair are shaped wide around the hips of the seated figure, before tapering in towards the base which finishes at the floor.

details: Roman, c.1st-4th century C.E. Purchased in 2012.
audio_description: A metal figurine of the deity Priapus. He is facing forward with an obviously enlarged and erect penis. He has a short beard and is wearing a toga-style draped tunic that is knee-length but gathers at the waist where it is held by both hands above the waist to expose the genitals. His legs are positioned together, and he is wearing shoes.

details: Cyprus, c.7th century B.C.E. Purchased in 1986.
audio_description: Humanoid clay figurine of beige colour. Modelling at the top of the head may represent either a short hairstyle or a headdress. The face is shaped with a long, pointed nose. Holes in the clay indicate eyes and a mouth. There is no indication of a chin; the head and neck seamlessly merge. The body is very loosely moulded, with the indication of arms and hands held inwards and against the body, made from pinched and folded clay. The lower body flares widely to an amorphous fluted shape. The object rests on a small black (modern) square plinth, held in place by short metal prongs on either side of the figurine base.

details: Egypt, Third Intermediate Period or Ptolemaic period, c. 1069 - 664 / 332 - 30 B.C.E. Donation, Prof. Naguib Kanawati, 1980.
audio_description: Moulded in faience, a teal-green glazed ceramic, this small amuletic figure is of the ancient Egyptian deity Pataikos. Represented as a standing, naked human male with dwarfism, the figure has a large head, arms beside the torso, slightly bent at the elbows, clenched fists, and legs bent so they are slightly apart at the knees. There is a loop behind the figure’s head, indicating that it may have been suspended from a string.

details: Unknown place of creation, 1930. Donation, Prof. Robin Walker, 1985.
audio_description: A white porcelain cup, with a long pouring spout and small handle. The top of the cup is half- enclosed on the spout side to enable the vessel to be tilted. There is a gold decorative line applied to the top of the vessel, outlining the rim. A gold line also runs down the side of the spout to the point at which it meets the cup wall, and a gold line is also observed on the vessel’s handle. The faded nature of this line may indicate frequent use of this object.

A likely wheel-made ceramic vessel. There is a handle arching over a flaring rim. The vessel has a narrow neck and wide, ovoid-shaped body tapering to a small circular base.  At the shoulder of the vessel is a spout, pointed upwards at an acute angle to allow the vessel to tilt. Several faded black painted lines can be seen as decoration around the handle, neck, and body. The spout was likely originally painted black in colour, although the surface is now eroded in places. The painted lines around the neck are tightly arranged, with a thick black line at the neck base. A thick, faded, wavy line extends around the shoulder of the vessel at the level of the spout.

A small, black ceramic vessel with an enclosed top featuring several perforated holes. The vessel features a narrow handle, thin pouring spout and a flat base.  In places, the applied black colouring is chipped, revealing orange coloured fired clay underneath.
